title: Co się stało?
note:
B1 Block 6 Situations unit — the spine's own line: 'telling what happened — recombining past, aspect, motion and connectives into short narratives.' Genuinely NEW: exactly one small closed chunk set built on the opaque past 3sg form stało (from stać się, 'to happen') — Co się stało? (What happened?), Coś się stało. (Something happened.), Nic się nie stało. (Nothing happened / never mind, the reassurance idiom). All three confirmed NEW via check_new.py before writing.

DESIGN FORK, logged (conservative default taken): stać się could have been opened as a real reflexive verb with its own conjugation slide, the way dziękuję and o której were reopened as real paradigm slots earlier in B1. Took the OTHER, more conservative precedent instead — the same opaque-block treatment nie słyszę and nie wiem got in a2_phone_func/a2_directions_func: stało is handed over as one closed word inside three fixed frames, never conjugated, no się-stać paradigm slide. Reasoning: this unit's job per the spine is recombination (connectives + already-owned past/aspect/motion), and opening a full new reflexive-verb paradigm on top of that would be two new systems in one unit — exactly the load-splitting rule AGENTS.md protects against. If James wants stać się opened as a real verb later, it is not blocked by anything here; this unit only closes off the three frames actually used.

coś (something) is a genuinely new word distinct from co (what, already taught) — not a homograph, but flagged so it is not read as the same word. Tagged individually per the every-form-taught rule since it appears inside coś się stało.

ZERO NEW STRUCTURES beyond re-declaring situation_chunk (house convention — every Situations unit re-declares it in teaches_structures even though the id itself was first taught back in leaf_shopping_a1, same pattern a2_phone_func and a2_wrapup_func both follow). Every narrative sentence recycles a structure already live on path: past_byc, past_isc, aspect_past, motion_prefixed (b1_arrive_leave's przyszedł, not the generic aspect_past twins — checked the owning pack's own teaches_structures before tagging, same check performed for b1_stories), past_plural, virile_past, byc_adj, negation, sie_reflexive, prep_do_gen, prep_w_loc, question.

SELF-VERIFICATION caught three near-misses before shipping, all via check_new.py: a first draft used musiałem/mogłem (past of musieć/móc) and czekałem (past of czekać) as narrative filler, assuming forms this common would already be taught — all three came back NEW (only the PRESENT of musieć/móc is taught; their past tense is not on the current spine at all). Also dropped ale ('but') from a draft sentence joining coś się stało and nic się nie stało — also NEW, no live pack teaches it. All three replaced with confirmed-taught alternatives (byłem zły instead of a musiałem clause; two short sentences instead of one ale-joined one). A fourth near-miss: an early nagle example used padał deszcz (weather past chunk) on the assumption the weather_chunk catalogue description covered it — check_new.py returned NEW, the exact same trap b1_stories's own note already flagged and fixed one unit ago on the same catalogue entry. Replaced with Nagle zgubiłem klucz. (aspect_past, confirmed taught).

Every recycled narrative form (byłem/byłam/był/była/byli/były, szedłem/szła, przyszedł, zgubiłem, kupiłem, mieszkali/mieszkały, pracowali/pracowały, spóźniłam się, oni/one, zły, po drodze, do domu/do pracy/w mieście/w domu/w szkole) verified TAUGHT via check_new.py against its owning pack before use, with no homograph risk found (zły is the same 'bad/wrong' sense trunk_adjectives_a1 already taught, not a different word).

intro.title: Co się stało? — the question that starts a story
intro.body:
Three fixed phrases share one word you have not seen before: stało. It comes from stać się, 'to happen' — but this unit does not open that verb up or conjugate it. Stało is handed over exactly the way nie słyszę and nie wiem were: one closed word, learned whole, inside three set frames.

Co się stało? asks the question — 'What happened?' Coś się stało says something happened, without saying what yet — coś ('something') is a new word, not the co ('what') you already have. Nic się nie stało is the reassurance — 'Nothing happened,' or in everyday use, 'It's fine, don't worry about it.'
intro.body_pl: Co się stało? Coś się stało. Nic się nie stało.

rows: opening a story, before the details

intro.title: Najpierw… Potem… Nagle… W końcu… — the words that build the story
intro.body:
Nothing new here — these six connectives are the ones you learned in the last unit. This slide is just the reminder that they are what actually turns separate sentences into one story: najpierw starts it, potem carries it forward, nagle is the twist, niestety and na szczęście mark whether the twist is bad or good, and w końcu closes it.

Every sentence you build with them uses a past-tense form you already own — byłem, szedłem, zgubiłem, przyszedł, byli — the connectives just decide the order they arrive in.
intro.body_pl: Najpierw byłem w pracy. Potem szedłem do domu. Nagle zgubiłem klucz. Niestety byłem zły. Na szczęście przyszedł brat. W końcu byłem w domu.

intro.body: Here is the full chain from the last slide, read as one story. Nothing in it is new except the way it is strung together — every sentence is a form you already had before this unit. Read it once before you start.

quiz.prompt: Your brother walks in looking upset, and you don't know why. You ask:
quiz.explain: Co się stało? is the question — you're asking what happened, not stating it.

quiz.prompt: Your friend seems different today and you're not sure why. You say:
quiz.explain: Coś się stało states it, without asking — 'something happened,' before you know what.

quiz.prompt: You bump into someone and they apologise nervously. You reassure them:
quiz.explain: This is the everyday 'it's fine, don't worry about it' — literally 'nothing happened.'

quiz.prompt: Byłem w pracy. ___ szedłem do domu.
quiz.explain: Potem carries the story to the next event — I was at work, then I was walking home.

quiz.prompt: Szedłem do domu i ___ zgubiłem klucz.
quiz.explain: Losing the key is the unexpected twist — nagle marks a sudden turn, not just the next step in order.
Being angry about a lost key is the bad turn — niestety, not its opposite na szczęście.
The brother arriving turns the story around for the better — na szczęście, the opposite of niestety.

quiz.prompt: ___ byłem w domu. (this is how the story ends)
quiz.explain: W końcu closes a story — the last thing that happened, after everything else.

quiz.prompt: ___ byłem w pracy. Potem szedłem do domu. (this is how the story begins)
quiz.explain: Najpierw opens a story — the first thing that happened, before potem takes over.
Same job as with byłem/szedłem earlier — potem moves a plural, virile story forward too.
